title: A Codimension-One Bound for the Singular Set of a Stationary Integral Varifold
coverage: Read all 7 sections (about 2600 lines). Section 2 (flat scales, Frostman measure, cone splitting): checked in detail. The monotonicity equality and the translation invariance of the cone along the span of spt λ are correct. The covering argument showing the support spans m directions uses s>m-1 correctly. Section 7 (abstract dimension reduction): re-derived every kernel identity by hand: A'=2A-D+R, D=∫ψ(y-x)·df, H'=2D, D²≤RH, P'=2P-n+q-2Pn≥(n-1)(n-2P). Checked the zero-height lemma, including the integrated lower bound P≥-(e^{2(t-t0)}-1)/8 and integrability of n leading to the contradiction with H→0. Checked the second blow-up: Egoroff plus monotonicity, the mass bounds via P'≥q/2-C, and limits along moving centers. Checked the equality case n=2P_0, q=n_0², the PSD null-vector argument giving (y-z)·f=n_0ν, and the spanning centers forcing f=0 and then ν=0. Section 6 (limit measure equations): checked the PSD block from |P_vh a|²≤B[a,a]. Derived ∇ν=2f, div f=d_0 and the stress identity from the test fields J_zY, |z|²J_zY and φz. Checked the signed-excess cell budget: floor a³, physical radius a^ζ ≤ b^κ since 3κ<ζ, and b=o(1) since ζ<1/m. Checked the physical-unit dilation d' that makes Λ=o(a²). Section 6b (density centers): verified the log-derivative formula for I_i and the absorption of adverse terms into the b'² positive term. Verified the Fubini averaging giving ε_i·O(a²)·∫_0^l t^{s-m}dt, with Fatou applied in the correct direction. Verified the translated-base expansion: the |w|² term is dropped with the correct sign, the cross term is killed by uniform centering, and div(P_h w)=H·w=o(a²). Section 5: checked the witness normalization and the exponents for curvature o(a_i) and first-moment o(a_i r_i^{m+1}). Also checked the subsolution and mean-value argument for |z|≤Ca. Section 4: followed the restart construction, the endpoint frequency bounds from the preceding and current failures, the ODE inward control, and the modified height identity (DY=P_h+O(ρ+|z|), which replaces AE's |z|≤Cρ²). These were checked at the level of logic and constants. I grepped the AE source (centering.tex) to confirm that its fit and failed-fit lemmas (ce:fit, ce:failed) do not use the multiplicity-defect hypothesis, as this paper claims; the defect is only used later, in the tent-control part of Prop ce:center, which this paper replaces with restarts. Not independently verified: AE's signed-excess theorem (Thm 3.1), scalar Lemma 2.5, and the detailed transfer of AE Lemmas 8.1–8.2 (collar/bulk estimates in Lemma 4.3). These are taken as inputs.
main_claim: Every stationary integral m-varifold in an open subset of R^{m+n} has dim_H Sing V ≤ m−1 (sharp). This resolves the Euclidean conjecture of Brena–Decio–De Lellis. The proof combines a Frostman measure of density-Q centers at flat scales, fitted centers with uniform frequency control on restart intervals, a centered height blow-up to measure-valued linear data (ν,f,β,m) satisfying 2m≤tr β, a curvature-compensated monotonicity averaged over centers (which needs s>m−1), and a measure-valued frequency dimension reduction.
sibling_notes: Sibling rank57 (AE, almost-everywhere regularity) reported no_gap_found but only skimmed AE's core barrier/merger and contact construction. This paper relies on AE's signed-excess theorem (Thm 3.1) and local fitting lemmas (7.1–7.2), so its correctness is conditional on those AE parts. I verified that the AE fit and failed-fit lemmas do not use the typical-point multiplicity-defect hypothesis that this paper drops.
